title: Kinematic Control and Dephasing Dynamics of Quantum Resources in $e^{+}e^{-}\toτ^{+}τ^{-}$
authors: Elhabib Jaloum, Omar Bachain, Mohamed Amazioug, Rachid Ahl Laamara
abstract: We characterize several quantum resources carried by the spins of the $τ^{+}τ^{-}$ pair produced in $e^{+}e^{-}$ annihilation. At the Belle-II energy, $\sqrt{s}=10.579\,\mathrm{GeV}$, Bell nonlocality, steerability, entanglement of formation, and coherence are governed by the production angle and are largest for transverse emission, $\vartheta=π/2$. Their common kinematic origin is exposed by expressing the spin state as a velocity and angle-dependent mixture of a separable contribution and a maximally entangled component. Within the physical production domain, this representation connects the weakly correlated threshold state at $\sqrt{s}=2m_τ$ to the Bell-state limit approached at ultrarelativistic energies. We then propagate the two-spin state through a phenomenological correlated-dephasing channel to determine how environmental memory and inter-channel classical correlations affect the available resources. Memory effects generate collapses and revivals that are absent from the monotonic Markovian evolution. The analysis therefore separates the kinematic mechanism that creates the spin correlations from the noise properties that control their subsequent survival.
summary: This work investigates the quantum correlations present in the spin state of $\tau^+\tau^-$ pairs created in $e^+e^-$ collisions. It quantifies these resources using multiple entanglement and nonlocality measures, showing they peak at transverse emission. Crucially, it models decoherence, demonstrating that environmental memory can cause revivals absent in simple Markovian decay.
main_problem: The paper characterizes quantum resources (nonlocality, entanglement, coherence) carried by the spins of $\tau^+\tau^-$ pairs produced in $e^+e^-$ annihilation and analyzes how these resources decay due to environmental decoherence.
main_result: The spin correlations exhibit a common kinematic origin connecting the threshold state to the Bell-state limit, and the decoherence analysis distinguishes between memory-generating non-Markovian revivals and simple Markovian decay.
method: The analysis uses quantum information diagnostics (CHSH, Concurrence, etc.) applied to the spin density matrix, followed by propagating the state through a phenomenological correlated-dephasing channel.
model_or_system: The system is the spin state of a $\tau^+\tau^-$ pair produced in $e^+e^-$ annihilation at $\sqrt{s}=10.579 \text{ GeV}$. The state is modeled as a two-qubit system evolving under both kinematic constraints and environmental noise.
key_observables: Bell nonlocality (CHSH), steerability, entanglement of formation (Concurrence), and coherence ($\mathcal{C}_{l1}$).
important_parameters: Production angle ($\vartheta$), center-of-mass energy ($\sqrt{s}$), and decoherence time scales ($\tau, \mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the Born-level reaction $e^+e^- \to \tau^+\tau^-$ and uses a phenomenological correlated-dephasing channel.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Feynman diagrams for production and show the temporal evolution of steering measures in both Markovian (rapid decay) and non-Markovian (oscillatory revivals) regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the kinematic dependence of quantum resources, showing their maximum at transverse emission. It then analyzes the evolution of these resources under decoherence, contrasting Markovian decay with non-Markovian memory effects.
why_interesting: The explicit separation of kinematic correlation generation from environmental noise dynamics provides a powerful framework for understanding resource preservation in particle physics processes.
